title: Mini-session tool mesh & typed-stream playbook (prd scratch)
content:
Context / motivation:
This is a lightweight, developer-friendly playbook for an incremental hosted-API surface that focuses on: mini-session semantics, a small tool-mesh for opportunistic tool invocation, and typed-stream frames for graceful partial/structured output. The goal is a pragmatic surface we can iterate on quickly and ship as an SDK + console guidance rather than a full protocol overhaul.

Problem statement (what breaks today):
- Large monolithic streaming frames or opaque partial text make client integration brittle for mobile/offline apps.
- Tool invocations are either synchronous/blocking or fully asynchronous with no compact resume semantics; developers need a middle ground for low-latency shortcuts (e.g., quick lookups) and stronger guarantees for long-running toollets.
- SDK ergonomics for partial/typed output are uneven: teams reinvent session resumption, fragmentation, and idempotency.

Goals / success metrics:
- Developer experience: provide a minimal SDK API for streaming typed frames + tool invocations with <1 day onboarding for a prototype integration.
- Reliability: enable graceful fallback from tool-mesh -> local fallback -> server-only response with measurable reduction in failed tool calls.
- Latency: sub-50ms initial frame delivered for cached/kv-prefetch paths on common flows.
- Observability: per-tool latency/cost breakdown exposed in console and available via SDK hooks.

Non-goals:
- Not a comprehensive session storage or full offline sync solution.
- Not locking in a heavyweight binary frame format; prefer JSON-lite or ndjson framing for now.

High-level proposal:
1) Mini-session identity: ephemeral session token (session_id) that lives for N minutes (default 15). Sessions support incremental snapshots (snapshot_id) and resume via resume_token. Sessions are cheap, signed tokens (no heavy server-side state unless client requests durability).

2) Typed-stream frames: small JSON objects streamed line-delimited (ndjson) with a compact union schema. Minimal frame types:
   - meta: session open/close, server hints
   - text: incremental text delta (patch or appended chunk) with seq numbers
   - typed: application-structured payloads (e.g., {type: "invoice", schema_version: "1.0", body: {...}})
   - tool_call: intent to invoke a tool or the response frame when the tool returns
   - checkpoint: a durable snapshot pointer (checkpoint_id) that clients can persist

   Example frame (single line):
   {"frame_type":"typed","seq":12,"payload":{"type":"search_result","schema":"v0.2","items":[{"title":"..."}]}}

3) Tool-mesh model: three tiers of tool execution for each tool_call frame (ordered by preference):
   - LOCAL_FAST: client-side shim or cached result (sdk-provided local adapter). Return immediate typed result if available.
   - EDGE_PREFETCH: prewarmed edge tooling (hosted short-lived workers or cached function results). Slight latency, low cost.
   - HOSTED_ASYNC: full server-side tool that may take longer; returns tool_call response frames when complete.

   Handshake: tool capability is advertised in the initial meta frame for the session (tool id, capability hints, fallback policy). SDK caches capability hints per session to avoid repeated negotiation.

4) Idempotency & observability: every tool_call must include a client-supplied call_id and an optional idempotency_key. The platform should emit trace events with route taken (LOCAL_FAST / EDGE / HOSTED) and a cost estimate. Instrumentation points: SDK hook on tool start/finish, console per-route breakdown, and sampling-enabled payload logs.

5) Graceful fallback semantics: clients should implement a 3-stage fallback model:
   - fast-path accept: if LOCAL_FAST exists, consume it and present.
   - speculative-render: if EDGE_PREFETCH is requested, SDK may display speculative UI and mark as provisional.
   - eventual-commit: when HOSTED_ASYNC return arrives, reconcile provisional UI. SDK exposes reconciliation callback and conflict resolution helpers.

6) SDK ergonomics (surface suggestions):
   - Small API: createSession(opts) -> session object with on('frame', handler) and send({type: 'user_input'}) and callTool(toolSpec, opts).
   - Helpers for typed frames: toTyped(schemaId, data) and parseTyped(frame) to reduce boilerplate.
   - Built-in local-adapter pattern: registerLocalTool(name, adapterFn) so integrators can plug-in instant shims for common ops.
   - Default reconcilers for text deltas and typed frames (merge strategy with seq handling).
   - Light offline caching: persist last checkpoint per session_id (opt-in) and allow resume with resume_token.

7) Streaming transport notes:
   - Keep to ndjson over HTTP streaming for v1: easy to debug, compatible with current streaming infra.
   - Binary framing (for perf) postponed to v2; ensure schema version included so clients can opt-in later.

Operational considerations:
- Backpressure: include windowing headers and per-session token budget to prevent long-lived sessions from hogging resources. SDK should surface on('backpressure') events.
- Autoscaling: tool-mesh EDGE workers should have scalable pools with a conservative fallback policy to HOSTED_ASYNC.
- Security: tool capability advertisement must respect org-level RBAC; do not include sensitive capability descriptors in client-visible meta for private deployments.
- Cost attribution: record which tier executed the tool for per-customer billing and cost dashboards.

Migration story for current customers:
- Provide a compatibility layer: server can produce both legacy partial-text streams and typed frames during a transition windows. SDKs support dual-parsing until customers opt-in.
- Quickstart: sample SDK snippet and a reference adapter for a common tool (calendar lookup).

Prototype checklist (MVP):
- [ ] ndjson typed-stream parser in JS SDK with on('frame') and default reconcilers.
- [ ] Local-tool adapter API + sample adapters (cache, quick-search).
- [ ] Server-side: meta frame + tool-call routing that implements the three-tier model (LOCAL simulated via stub).
- [ ] Console: per-session view showing tool routing and cost traces.
- [ ] E2E example app (chat + calendar lookup) demonstrating speculative-render and eventual-commit.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How big should a session resume_token be? Security vs convenience.
- Idempotency collision handling across multi-device resume. Use strong idempotency_key (UUID) recommendations in SDK.
- Backwards compatibility cost: shipping dual streams increases server complexity. Is staged rollout via SDK opt-in sufficient?
- Do we want schema registry for typed frames (hosted service) vs namespaced version strings in payload?

Risks:
- Over-ambitious: trying to support too many fallback modes could complicate SDK. Keep initial SDK tiny; expose primitives not policies.
- UX complexity: speculative UI patterns are subtle; provide reference UI components and guidance in dev docs.

Next steps / owners:
- Product: validate core API surface with 3 partner integration teams (owners: Aisha Khan, Elena Ortiz).
- Eng: prototype JS SDK parser + local-adapter (owner: Marcus Li).
- Applied ML / runtime: experiment with edge-prefetch heuristics and trace instrumentation (owner: Ravi Patel).
- Docs: draft quickstart, sample app, and console wireframe (owner: Elena).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact — looking for feedback on the three-tier tool mesh, the typed-frame union shape, and minimal SDK primitives.
- Please call out any hard constraints from infra (long-lived streaming cost, existing tracing hooks) that would change the design.
plain_text_preview: Mini-session tool mesh & typed-stream playbook (prd scratch) - draft by Aisha Khan. Focus: session tokens, ndjson typed frames, three-tier tool routing (local/edge/hosted), minimal SDK API, speculative-render UX, and incremental migration plan. Open questions: schema registry, idempotency across resumes, backpressure policies.
